newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says NDF dlr sales need prior approval.
newsitem.headline: Manila says NDF dlr sales need prior approval.

text.p: All non-deliverable forward contracts of onshore banks to sell dollars to non-residents, with immediate effect, must have prior approval from the Philippine central bank, a circular released on Wednesday said.
The new circular is effective for three months.
Central bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Tuesday the rule effectively banned NDF dollar sales since the bank was unlikely to approve any new contract during the three month period.

"In order to curb undue speculations in the foreign exchange market, all forward contracts to sell foreign exchange to non-residents (including offshore banking units) with no full delivery of principal, including cancellations, roll-overs/renewals thereof shall be submitted for prior clearance to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (Philippine central bank)," the circular, dated July 22, said.
The ruling will be reviewed after three months.
In a separate circular, the central bank ordered all banks with outstanding NDFs, either to sell or purchase dollars, as of July 17 to report an inventory by the end of the week.
Weekly reports are also required starting next week.
At present, eight banks with derivative licences can trade in NDFs.
